reasoning_traces.think:
The core operators—relative joint coordinates, kinematic derivatives, and posture vector aggregation—are derived from multi-modal sensor data (RGB-D, LiDAR, 360° camera) to classify indoor human activities. These features form a structured input space where each posture is represented as a vector of distances from a torso reference. Velocity and acceleration are computed numerically from these coordinates, enabling motion-aware classification. The aggregation step combines temporal sequences into fixed-size matrices for machine learning. The failure modes include sensor limitations (e.g., occlusion, poor RGB-D silhouette recognition), lack of contextual awareness (e.g., inability to distinguish texting while walking from carrying), and absence of temporal modeling. These primitives do not generalize to NFL outcomes due to domain mismatch: HAR focuses on static poses and motion dynamics, whereas GSE requires predictive modeling of strategic, sequential, and probabilistic game events.
